To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Noether’s first (conservation) and second (gauge) theorems can be formulated in the general setting of reducilbe graded Lagrangian theory, that the latter theory is characterized by higher-stage Noether and BRST operators that are related by a cochain sequence, and that Noether’s second theorem associates to a gauge symmetry a consered current which is proved by the global variational principle to be a total derivative.

the first and second Noether theorems can be formulated in a general context of Grassmann-graded degenerate Lagrangian theory, and that the first theorem is a straightforward corollory of the global variatonal formula.
Noether’s first theorems are a corollary of Noether’s second theorem, which in its turn can be derived as a corollary from the global variational principle.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the theory of Noether’s theorems in the framework of reducible graded Lagrangian theory, and the application of these results to the construction of BRST extensions of Lagrangian systems with higher-stage gauge symmmetries.
a systematic investigation of the Noether identities of a general reducible graded Lagrangian theory in order to obtain the corresponding Noether theorems.
a generalization of the Noether theorems for Lagrangian systems of odd variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Noether identities and the Noether currents are nothing more than a consequence of the global variation principle.
the Noether identities and the Noether theorems for reducible Lagrangian systems are obtained as corollaries of the global variatonal formula.
the global variational principle, Noether’s first, second, and third theorems are equivalent and that they are the basic principles of the variational calculus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Noether’s first, second and BRST extensions are all derived from the same global variational principle.

the higher-stage Noether symmetries of a Lagrangian system are defined by the cohomological ascent operator of the Koszul– Tate complex of higher-stage Noethers identities, and that the associated conserved currents are given by the global variational formulas.

the Noether identities are the necessary and sufficient conditions for gauge invariance of the action and the conserved currents are the necessary and only sufficient conditions for the existence of gauge symmetries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Noether’s second theorem and its BRST extension are not a corollary of Noether’s first one but rather an independent result.
reducible Lagrangian systems are naturally equipped with an intrinsic hierarchy of gauge symmetries and conserved currents.
Noether’s first two theorems are not two distinct results, but two sides of the same coin.
